title.narrative: Strengthening the Resilience and Adaptive Capacity of Communities to Climate Change (SRA4C)

description.narrative: The "Strengthening the Resilience of Communities to Climate Change (SR3C)" project has been implemented in the Semen Balesa and Dubancho kebeles, Lemo woreda, Hadiya zone, Central Ethiopia Regional State for the last 17 months (from November 1st, 2022, to March 31st, 2024). The project has accomplished most of the intended activities and met the set objectives. An evaluation conducted by an independent consultant, CAE, and the EECMY DASSC, revealed that the project has performed well and significantly benefited the target communities. Both evaluations, external and government, indicated that there are remining development gaps and recommended the continuation of the project in the area. Based on the recommendations from the evaluation and requests from the community and local/woreda sectors, the EECMY DASSC and Christian Aid (CA) were committed to continue implementing the project with few modifications on the initial phase. With a title “Strengthening the Resilience and Adaptive Capacity of Communities to Climate Change (SRA4C) in Central Ethiopia Reion, Hadiya Zone, Lemo Woreda", the project will be implemented in three kebeles namely, Semen Belesa, Dubancho and Dijo Damala Kebele’s. The second phase will be implemented for 12 months, from 01 July 2024 to 30 Jun 2025. The project aims to contribute to the improvement of community well-being in Lemo Woreda, Hadiya zone, within the Central Ethiopia Regional State. The project is financially supported by Christian Aid and will be implemented by the EECMY DASSC through its South-Central Synod branch office (SCS BO). The project will employ a participatory approach, where all key stakeholders - including the local community, government, community institutions (FBOs, CBOs), and others - will actively participate in the planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation processes. To enhance the food security situation of the target communities, the project will focus on the following key activities: 1.Improving crop production and productivity of the target households 2.Promoting biological and physical soil and water conservation through natural resource management (NRM) 3.Enhancing the socio-economic condition of poor women in the target areas A total budget of ETB 3,413,192 (GBP 46,438) is proposed for the implementation of the planned project activities. Through these interventions, the project aims to reach 280 households (90 female-headed) with a total population of 1,400 (685 male and 715 female). The participatory approach and the focus on improving food security, natural resource management, and women's socio-economic empowerment are well-aligned with the overall goal of contributing to the improvement of community well-being in Lemo Woreda. With effective implementation, the project has the potential to make a positive impact on the target communities.
